prompt:
Create ONE 2D animation character pose asset for shot S09 of the short film "来电". Use the two attached images to preserve the exact identity and drawing style of Xiaoman, the young girl in the yellow dress. Reference 1 is her approved full-body character, reference 2 is her expression sheet. Create only the first holding pose (A), not a slap pose, not an action sheet.

Scene/action: Xiaoman is kneeling naturally and sitting back on her folded legs, facing screen RIGHT in a clear side view with a small amount of three-quarter visibility. She holds ONE small old-fashioned metal flashlight with BOTH hands in front of her torso, looking down at the switch with a puzzled "why won't this turn on?" expression. Slightly knitted eyebrows, a small uncertain mouth, attentive eyes; she is not smiling or crying. The flashlight is OFF. Her head, hair tufts and ponytails, complete figure, knees, red sandals, both hands and the entire flashlight must fit inside the image with a safe margin.

Identity: identical round child face, dark brown eyes, short straight fringe, one curved tuft at the crown, two low pigtails with red fluffy pom-pom ties. The far pigtail may be partly hidden in the side view. Yellow short-sleeved dress with simple white polka dots, white rounded Peter Pan collar, the same red strapped sandals as the reference. Keep the established child proportions and costume, clean fine dark outlines, simple flat cel colors and restrained fabric folds. No photorealism, no dramatic illumination.

Natural pose: torso leans forward just a little toward the flashlight, hips resting over the folded legs, knees comfortably together in front, lower legs folded behind, feet and red sandals anatomically readable. The dress drapes naturally over her lap and knees. No stool, no chair, no cross-legged pose, no standing pose, no floating hips, no twisted knees or duplicated legs.

Flashlight design follows the existing film prop: a compact vintage tin flashlight about 19 cm long, slim cylindrical faded brick-red metal body approximately 3.6 cm across, small silver tail cap at the LEFT, slightly wider flared chrome/silver head approximately 5.6 cm across at the RIGHT, and a narrow dull blue-gray glass lens facing RIGHT. A small black SLIDING SWITCH sits on a silver mount on top of the middle of the red body. Modest worn paint marks only, no text or branding. It is a real handheld cylindrical flashlight, not a lantern, not a rectangular device, not a large searchlight. Show the complete prop nearly horizontal, with the head only slightly tilted upward. Do NOT show any light beam, glow, illuminated lens, light pool, spark, or lantern post.

Two normal child arms and exactly two natural child hands cooperate in a believable grip. The NEAR anatomical RIGHT hand grips the rear/middle red cylinder, with her right thumb resting directly on the top sliding switch, ready to push it; the fingers curve naturally around and under the cylinder. The FAR anatomical LEFT hand supports the forward cylinder just behind the wider chrome head from underneath. Leave a clear readable relationship between the two wrists and the flashlight. The cylindrical barrel passes through the palms' grips, the fingertips wrap around it with correct front/back occlusion; fingers must not float outside the cylinder, stretch into long bars, overlap as extra hands, merge together, or pass through solid metal. Normal short thumb and finger lengths. Do not copy any deformed procedural hand design. Do not add bracelets.

One isolated full-body girl and one flashlight ONLY. Plain uniform light gray background with neutral flat light. No room, floor line, cast shadow, furniture, drawer, lamp, extra people, extra objects, text, labels, border or collage. Landscape 1536x1024 if supported, character fills most of the height; retain native output dimensions.
